---
title: Contributing
---

Keep each authored skill authoritative and self-contained. Installation of
one directory must provide every required local reference and asset.

1. Add `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter. Use a
   lowercase hyphenated name matching the directory.
2. Put required companions inside that directory and link them relatively
   from the skill. Avoid required references to repository-level docs or
   uninstalled skills. Include the applicable license with distributed files.
3. Add `{name: <name>, file: skills/<name>/SKILL.md}` to the `skill.skills` list
   in the root `great-docs.yml`. This is the explicit publication allowlist.
4. Add a small human-facing page in `docs/` explaining setup, examples, and
   limitations, with a link to the authoritative skill. Do not copy its
   procedure into the page.
5. Run validation, build, and the isolated installer checks described in the
   [README](https://github.com/butterlyn/engineering-skills#readme), then open a PR
   or push to `main`.

Pull requests validate and build without publishing. Pushes to `main` validate,
build, check the uploaded Pages artifact, deploy, and verify the live content.
The workflow uses the committed Python lockfile and pinned tooling. Generated
HTML stays out of Git.

The pinned Great Docs release reads `great-docs.yml` at the repository root and
writes `great-docs/_site`. Its explicit multi-skill mode copies companions.
The build helper normalizes Windows manifest separators to URL paths, stamps
the source revision, and validates the result; Great Docs still generates
the site and discovery manifest.
It also removes the release's links to absent API-only `llms` outputs in this
documentation-only project.

Upgrade documentation dependencies intentionally with `uv lock`, review the
lockfile, and rerun the full checks. Review upstream Matt Pocock dependencies
separately in the [curation record](https://github.com/butterlyn/engineering-skills/blob/main/CURATION.md).
